# Working Agreements

> This document records the concrete practices your team agrees to follow
> while developing, reviewing, integrating, and verifying the system.
> Update it when experience shows that an agreement needs to change.

## Communication Practices

<!-- Examples of questions to resolve:
     - Where does routine team communication occur?
     - How quickly should messages normally be acknowledged?
     - How are blockers communicated? -->

## Work Planning and Ownership

<!-- How will work be assigned?
     How will ownership and status be visible?
     What should happen when someone becomes blocked? -->

## Git and Branching

<!-- Define your team's branch and repository practices.
     Consider direct commits to main, branch naming, and keeping branches current. -->

## Commits

<!-- What makes a useful commit?
     What expectations do you have for commit size and messages? -->

## Pull Requests and Review

<!-- When is a pull request required?
     Who reviews?
     What must be true before a PR can be merged? -->

## Testing and Verification

<!-- What testing is expected before work is considered complete?
     Who is responsible for verifying changes? -->

## Definition of Done

<!-- Define what "done" means for your team.
     Consider implementation, testing, integration, documentation,
     review, traceability, and known limitations. -->

## Documentation and Traceability

<!-- What documentation must remain current?
     How will requirements, decisions, code, tests, and evidence be linked? -->

## AI-Assisted Work

<!-- What must a team member do before accepting AI-generated code,
     tests, documentation, or engineering recommendations? -->

## Handling Defects and Broken Builds

<!-- What happens when someone discovers a defect?
     What happens if main or CI is broken? -->

## Working Agreement Changes

<!-- How can the team change these agreements?
     Record significant changes rather than silently changing practices. -->
